tasks.gr12-advanced-databases-sql-t2: Topic: Advanced Databases and SQL. Cover tables, primary keys, foreign keys, SELECT queries with criteria, sorting, aggregate functions, GROUP BY, and safe INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE operations. Ask Grade 12 learners to trace query results, choose suitable data types and explain how structured data supports reliable applications.
tasks.gr12-relational-data-joins-normalisation: Topic: Relational Data, Joins and Normalisation. Cover one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many relationships, join logic, linking or junction tables, referential integrity and normalisation to reduce redundancy. Ask Grade 12 learners to interpret schemas, choose suitable joins and explain why poor design causes duplication and anomalies.
tasks.gr12-forms-reports-database-program-inte: Topic: Forms, Reports and Database Program Integration. Cover forms for data capture, lookup controls, validation in forms, reports for grouped output, parameter-driven queries and integrating program code with a database connection. Ask Grade 12 learners to reason about input accuracy, output design and reliable program-database workflows.
tasks.gr12-networks-security-systems-integrati: Topic: Networks, Security and Systems Integration. Cover LANs and WANs, routers and switches, TCP/IP ideas, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, authentication, encryption, firewalls, malware threats and system integration through connected services. Ask Grade 12 learners to match technologies to scenarios and recommend secure communication practices.
tasks.gr12-ai-vr-ar-mr-t2: Topic: AI, VR, AR and MR. Cover what artificial intelligence is and is used for, its advantages, disadvantages and limitations (data, bias, errors), and what virtual, augmented and mixed reality are, with their hardware, advantages and limitations. Keep the content factual and do not name products as the answer. Ask Grade 12 learners to tell VR, AR and MR apart, give a use, or state a limitation.
tasks.gr12-computer-criminals-cybercrime-t2: Topic: Computer Criminals and Cybercrime. Cover hackers, crackers (ethical hackers), cyber gangs and virus authors, types and effects of cybercrime (hardware, software, information, identity, bandwidth, time and services, scams), worms, malware, denial of service, back doors, phishing, botnets, safeguards, and the right to access versus the right to privacy. Describe only: no instructions for committing any attack. Ask Grade 12 learners to define a term, recognise a type of crime, or choose a safeguard.
